hits.story: 33 major US companies oppose tokenized versions of their stocks on OKX/ICE
hits.draft_en:
33 big US companies now object to tokenized versions of their stock on the OKX/ICE venue.

IBM, Microsoft, JPMorgan, Alphabet and more.

That tells you something simple.
A tokenized stock still depends on the issuer, the venue and the law.

$BTC doesn't have an issuer that can object.

So what are you actually buying with a tokenized share, the stock or a promise about it?
Save this / repost it for the next 'everything goes on-chain' thread.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Objecting is the easy part. The real question is what it changes.

Does an objection block the listing, or just put it on record? Without that detail it's hard to tell if this is a wall or a speed bump.
hits.video_tip: Logos stacking up to 33 next to a single $BTC icon with 'no issuer'; 8s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Ask what the objection legally does (block vs just disclose; check the OKX/ICE 30-day objection window) and contrast issuer-dependent tokens with $BTC having no issuer.
hits.why_chosen: Biggest debate of the day with a clear question to ask; lets him contrast issuer risk with $BTC spot.

hits.name: Michael Saylor
hits.text: $MSTR shareholders have approved the Daily Dividends amendment. Preliminary results show 99.3% of votes cast were in favor. The amendment enables $STRF, $STRC, $STRK and $STRD to accrue dividends every calendar day. Thank you to all who voted. https://t.co/w1Cp4GKUy5

hits.story: Strategy preferreds get daily dividends
hits.draft_en:
Strategy's preferred stocks will now accrue dividends every day, after a 99.3% shareholder vote (preliminary).

Worth being clear on what that is:
- a claim on a company that holds $BTC
- paid in dollars, by that company
- not bitcoin, and not your keys

Yield always comes from somewhere.
Here it's the issuer's ability to keep paying.

Would you hold the preferred or the coin?
Save this before someone calls it 'Bitcoin yield'.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Daily accrual changes the payment schedule, not the source of the payment.

Honest question: what happens to these dividends in a long $BTC drawdown? Has anyone modeled the coverage?
hits.video_tip: Split screen: a coin in a hardware wallet vs. a share certificate, caption 'which one is bitcoin?'; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Separate the instrument from the asset: a preferred is a company's dollar obligation; ask how coverage holds up in a deep $BTC drawdown (check the filings).
hits.why_chosen: Huge reach with a product most readers confuse with holding BTC; room for a clear custody/risk distinction.

Repost if someone in LatAm needs this framing.

The real question for a saver there: dollars, $BTC, or both, and in what mix?

hits.hook: 🚨 ALERT: CZ warns leaked exchange data can fuel phishing, SIM swaps and real-world attacks after four reported leaks across crypto and TradFi.
hits.draft_en:
CZ: leaked exchange data can fuel phishing, SIM swaps and real-world attacks. Four leaks reported across crypto and TradFi.

The part people skip:
your coins can be safe and you can still be a target.

KYC data doesn't expire. Once it leaks, it's out.

What you can control:
- separate email for exchanges
- no SMS 2FA
- withdraw what you don't trade

What would you add?
Repost so someone turns off SMS 2FA today.
hits.draft_quote_en:
'Stay SAFU' is advice. The structural problem is that exchanges hold data you can't rotate like a password.

How many of these leaks came from vendors, not the exchange itself? Coinbase's latest was via Amplitude. Worth tracking.
hits.video_tip: ID card sliding out of an exchange icon into a phishing email. 8s.
hits.reply_angle: Point out leaked KYC data can't be rotated and suggest checking how many recent leaks came through third-party vendors (e.g. Coinbase via Amplitude).
hits.why_chosen: Security warning with a practical gap; invites a checklist reply.

glassnode: since January, only five daily closes above it, never more than three in a row.

Resistance tells you where. Not when.

hits.name: Jack Mallers
hits.text:
My dad always said: for everything in life, even gold, more demand finds more supply.

He was right. Until bitcoin. https://t.co/39k7B5kICT
hits.hook: My dad always said: for everything in life, even gold, more demand finds more supply.
hits.story: More demand, more supply, except bitcoin
hits.draft_en:
'More demand finds more supply. Even gold. Until bitcoin.'

The supply side is true: 21M cap, issuance set in code.

But fixed supply doesn't fix the price.
With supply fixed, demand swings hit price directly.
That's part of why $BTC drawdowns are so deep.

Scarcity is the feature. Volatility is the cost.
Are you sized for both?
If it was useful, a repost helps more people see it.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Fixed supply, agreed.

The other side: when demand drops, supply can't adjust either. Fixed supply means demand alone sets the price, both ways.
hits.video_tip: Gold mine output rising vs. a flat 21M line, then a price line swinging; 12s.
hits.reply_angle: Add the missing half: inelastic supply means demand shocks go straight to price; point to past $BTC drawdowns as the cost of scarcity.
hits.why_chosen: Clean scarcity claim with good saves; room to add the volatility side.

hits.text:
THREE NEW BITCOIN CORE VULNERABILITIES DISCOVERED, INCLUDING BUG ALLOWING ATTACKERS TO REMOTELY CRASH NODES

hits.hook: THREE NEW BITCOIN CORE VULNERABILITIES DISCOVERED, INCLUDING BUG ALLOWING ATTACKERS TO REMOTELY CRASH NODES
hits.story: Three Bitcoin Core vulnerabilities disclosed
hits.draft_en:
Three Bitcoin Core vulnerabilities disclosed, one lets malicious peers crash some nodes, per BitcoinNews.com.

If you run a node, the practical part:
- check which versions are affected
- update from the official release
- verify the signatures before installing

Public disclosure after a fix is how open source is supposed to work.
The risk is people who never update.

When did you last update your node?
Save this for your next node maintenance.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Useful to know which versions are affected and whether the fixes are already in a release.

Any link to the official disclosure? That's what node runners should read, not the headline.
hits.video_tip: Terminal screen: version check, update, signature verification, done; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Point people to the official Bitcoin Core disclosure: affected versions, fixed release, and verifying signatures before updating (check the release notes).
hits.why_chosen: Security news with a concrete action for node runners; fits his autonomy and verification angle.

hits.story: $BTC 6x in six years (CoinMarketCap snapshot)
hits.draft_en:
$BTC was $13,031 six years ago this week. Today about $80,481. 6x.

Looks clean. It wasn't.

In between there were deep drawdowns, a bear market and months of chop.
The return was there. Holding through it was the hard part.

And half of those top-10 coins aren't top-10 anymore.

Would you have held through the worst drawdown?
Save this for the next 'I should've bought' moment.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Point to point returns hide the path.

What was the max drawdown between those two dates? That's the number that decides who actually got the 6x.
hits.video_tip: Six-year $BTC line with the two endpoints glowing, then the drawdowns highlighted in red; 12s.
hits.reply_angle: Point-to-point hides the path: ask for the max drawdown and time underwater between the two dates (check price history) and note survivorship (5 of 10 coins left the top 10).
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + $BTC price over the last six years with the start ($13,031) and today ($80,481) marked and drawdowns shaded; series to be pulled. Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Clean point-to-point number begging for the drawdown and survivorship context.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
A dip below the 50-week moving average after a sharp rally isn’t necessarily bearish.

Same pattern in 2023, and BTC gained 49% over the next 30 days. https://t.co/jvy590DBJg
hits.hook: A dip below the 50-week moving average after a sharp rally isn’t necessarily bearish.
hits.story: BTC dip below the 50-week MA
hits.draft_en:
'A dip below the 50-week average isn't bearish. Same pattern in 2023, then +49% in 30 days.'

Maybe. But that's one example.

Before trusting a setup:
- how many times did it happen?
- what was the median result, not the best one?
- how many times did it fail?

One chart is a story. A sample is evidence.

Anyone have the full list of 50-week MA breaks for $BTC?
Save this for the next 'same pattern as' chart.
hits.draft_quote_en:
One instance from 2023 isn't a base rate.

How many times has $BTC closed below the 50-week MA after a rally, and what did the next 30 days look like in each case? The median would say more than the best one.
hits.video_tip: Overlay several 50-week MA breaks on one chart, then highlight only 2023 to show cherry-picking; 12s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Turn the n=1 claim into a base rate: list every $BTC close below the 50-week MA after a rally and check the median 30-day return (backtest to run, don't quote a figure).
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + every weekly $BTC close below the 50-week MA after a rally, with the following 30-day return for each case (median marked); price history to be checked. Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Single-example pattern claim with big reach; ideal for a base-rate check he can actually run.

hits.name: Natalie Brunell ⚡️
hits.hook: “Bitcoin would be thrown into total disarray...”
hits.story: AI vs. quantum risk to public keys
hits.draft_en:
AI breaking public key encryption vs. quantum risk: nic_carter's take is getting shared today.

Before panicking, separate the questions:
- what is actually broken today?
- which coins have exposed public keys?
- what would an upgrade path look like?

The practical part: reused or old addresses carry more exposure.

Which of these do you think is underrated?
Want me to go deeper on any part?
hits.draft_quote_en:
Worth separating 'possible someday' from 'broken today'.

What is the concrete attack he's describing, and how many coins sit in addresses with exposed public keys?
hits.video_tip: Padlock with two shadows labeled AI and quantum, caption 'which one is real?'; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Ask for specifics: which attack, which coins (exposed public keys, reused addresses), and what timeline; avoid fear without evidence.
hits.why_chosen: Open debate with many replies and saves; room for a clarifying, evidence-first reply.

hits.hook: $82K is a clear “Buy” signal for bitcoin:native , just as $63K was. https://t.co/fJIQ0D5OX4 https://t.co/r5IKEAEUdz
hits.draft_en:
"$82K is a buy signal, just like $63K was."

Maybe.

But a signal that's only shown when it worked isn't a signal yet.

What I'd want to see:
- every time it fired
- how many times it failed
- the drawdown after each one

Spot only, no leverage, and the misses on the table.

Would you buy $BTC on this?
Bookmark it for when the next 'clear buy' shows up.
hits.draft_quote_en:
$63K worked. What about the times it fired and didn't?

Show me the full list of signals, hits and misses, and the max drawdown after each. Then it's a signal.
hits.video_tip: Chart with green 'buy' dots, then grey dots fade in for the misses. 8s.
hits.reply_angle: Survivorship check: ask for every past firing of the signal, including misses and drawdowns, before treating $82K as a buy.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + BTC price with every past firing of the cited buy signal marked, hits and misses, plus drawdown after each; data to be checked from the source. Navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Bold 'clear buy' call with only one past example; strong room for a hit-rate question.

hits.name: Dan Held
hits.text: If your financial advisor hasn't recommended Bitcoin yet, fire them.
hits.hook: If your financial advisor hasn't recommended Bitcoin yet, fire them.
hits.story: Fire your advisor if no Bitcoin
hits.draft_en:
'If your advisor hasn't recommended Bitcoin, fire them.'

I'd ask a different question first:
- did they explain the drawdowns? (check 2018, 2022)
- did they talk about custody?
- did they size it to your situation?

An advisor who says 'buy' without that is worse than one who says 'not yet'.

What would you want them to explain?
Save this before your next advisor meeting.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Recommending it isn't the test. Explaining sizing, drawdowns and custody is.

An advisor who says 'buy' and stops there isn't better.
hits.video_tip: Three-question checklist appearing over an office meeting scene; 10s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Reframe the test: what matters is whether the advisor explains sizing, past drawdowns and custody, not whether they say 'buy'.
hits.why_chosen: Provocative one-liner with lots of replies; easy to add a practical checklist.

President Trump reportedly plans to hit Iran's nuclear sites and infrastructure once the elections are over. https://t.co/VIV32QJilA
hits.hook: JUST IN: 🇺🇸 U.S. has warned Gulf allies to prepare for an intense renewal of the Iran war after the midterms.
hits.story: Reported US warning to Gulf allies on Iran
hits.draft_en:
"Reportedly" is doing a lot of work in geopolitical headlines.

For a $BTC spot holder, the practical questions:
- is this confirmed by more than one source?
- how did $BTC trade after past escalation headlines?
- does it change your plan, or just your mood?

A rule written in a calm week beats a reaction to a headline.
Save this for the next scary headline.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Single-source "reportedly" story. Worth waiting for confirmation.

And for markets: what did $BTC actually do in the weeks after past escalation headlines? Has anyone checked the base rate instead of guessing?
hits.video_tip: Headline on screen, stamp 'reportedly', then 'what does your rule say?' 8s.
hits.reply_angle: Event-study angle: check BTC returns after past Middle East escalation headlines instead of assuming risk-off; flag it's single-source.
hits.why_chosen: Geopolitical headline with replies and quotes; room for an event-study / base-rate angle without taking sides.

hits.name: Documenting ₿itcoin 📄
hits.text: How the cryptography of Bitcoin works https://t.co/FrEzkJLJeX
hits.hook: How the cryptography of Bitcoin works https://t.co/FrEzkJLJeX
hits.story: How Bitcoin cryptography works
hits.draft_en:
Most people holding $BTC can't explain what their keys actually do.

You don't need the math. You need three ideas:
- private key: signs
- public key: lets others verify
- seed: the backup of all of it

Lose the seed, lose access.
Share the seed, lose the coins.

What part of custody confused you most at first?
Save this for whoever you're onboarding.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Good one to share.

What's the one cryptography concept you think every self-custody user should understand before buying their first sat?
hits.video_tip: Three cards: key signs, pubkey verifies, seed backs up; 9:16, 12s.
hits.reply_angle: Ask which concept self-custody users get wrong most often, and add the practical link: what a seed backup protects and what it doesn't.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [explanatory image] + simple diagram private key, public key, address and seed with one line each, no figures. Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Educational post, easy to complement with a custody angle (content is a video link, not read).

hits.story: Fed holds rates, 10-2 vote
hits.draft_en:
The Fed held rates at 3.75%-4.00%. Two dissents wanted a hike.

The headline is 'no change'.
The signal might be the dissents.

For $BTC spot holders, the useful question:
- does a hold move price a week later?
- or is it noise around a trend?

I'd check the base rate before reacting.

What are you watching after today's decision?
If it was useful, a repost helps more people see it.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Two votes for a hike says more than the hold itself.

Has $BTC behaved differently after meetings with hawkish dissents? That would be worth checking before reading anything into today.
hits.video_tip: 'Hold' stamp on screen, then zoom to '10-2' and two hawkish dissents; 8s.
hits.reply_angle: Point to the dissents and suggest a base-rate check: $BTC returns a week after holds with hawkish dissents vs. other holds (data to run).
hits.why_chosen: Fed decision in Spanish for his LatAm audience; dissents give a concrete angle to test.

The crypto asset manager projects annualized returns of 34.3% over the next decade, driven by institutional adoption and limited https://t.co/P8cXFJ32iu
hits.hook: THE BLOCK: Bitwise has raised its bitcoin bitcoin:native price target to $1.6 million by 2036, up from its previous $1.3 million forecast for 2035.
hits.story: Bitwise $1.6M BTC target by 2036
hits.draft_en:
Bitwise raised its $BTC target to $1.6M by 2036, per The Block.

A 10-year price target is a model, not a forecast you can check soon.

What matters is the inputs:
- how much institutions allocate
- how fast that happens
- what supply is actually liquid

Change one input and the number moves a lot.

Which assumption do you trust least?
If this helps you read the next target, a repost spreads it.
hits.draft_quote_en:
The interesting part isn't $1.6M, it's the allocation assumption behind it.

What does the model give if institutions allocate half of what Bitwise assumes? Is that scenario published?
hits.video_tip: Slider animation: change the allocation assumption and watch the 2036 target swing; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Ask for the sensitivity: which allocation and adoption inputs drive the $1.6M, and what the target is if they come in at half (check the Bitwise report).
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + scenario bars for the 2036 target under different institutional allocation assumptions, taken only from the Bitwise report (to be checked). Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Big round target with hidden assumptions; room for a model-inputs question rather than hype.

hits.story: On-chain activity flat vs. the Calacanis debate
hits.draft_en:
Bulls answering Calacanis keep citing rising on-chain activity.
Santiment says weekday $BTC transactions look flat vs. July to September.

That doesn't mean bears are right.
It means one argument doesn't hold.

Better question:
- what metric would actually lead price?
- has it worked out of sample?

Which on-chain metric do you trust, and why?
Save this before the next 'on-chain is booming' post.
hits.draft_quote_en:
This is the right way to answer a bet: check the claim, not the vibes.

Worth adding: has transaction count ever led $BTC price reliably? If not, it's a weak argument for either side.
hits.video_tip: Two quotes, 'on-chain is booming' vs. a flat transaction line, then 'check the data'; 9:16, 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Add the next step: test whether transaction count has ever led $BTC price (lagged correlation check to run), so the debate moves from vibes to evidence.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + weekday $BTC transaction count, Oct 14-27 vs. July-September average, as reported by Santiment (to be checked). Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Data post that tests a popular narrative; perfect for a quant follow-up question.

hits.name: The Bitcoin Conference
hits.text:
#BITCOIN GOOGLE SEARCHES JUST HIT A 5-YEAR LOW WHILE BTC SITS AT $80,600 🤫

WE'RE STILL EARLY! 🙌 https://t.co/JG85XkzSMl
hits.hook: #BITCOIN GOOGLE SEARCHES JUST HIT A 5-YEAR LOW WHILE BTC SITS AT $80,600 🤫
hits.story: Google searches for Bitcoin at 5-year low
hits.draft_en:
Google searches for Bitcoin at a 5-year low while $BTC sits near $80K, per a post going around today.

'Still early' is one read.
Another: retail attention lags price, and low interest can last.

Search interest is a sentiment gauge, not a timing tool.

What I'd check:
- past lows in search interest
- $BTC 6 and 12 months later
- how often low interest stayed low

Save this for the next time someone says 'still early'.
hits.draft_quote_en:
5-year low in searches, per the post. Does low search interest have a track record as a buy signal, or does it just mean retail isn't watching?

Would like to see the past lows and what $BTC did 6 and 12 months after.
hits.video_tip: Search-interest line falling while price stays flat, caption 'early or ignored?'; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Ask for the base rate: check past Google Trends lows and $BTC returns 6-12 months later before calling it 'early'.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + 5-year Google Trends interest for 'Bitcoin' overlaid on $BTC price, marking past search lows; data from Google Trends and price history, to be checked. Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Debatable 'still early' claim on a sentiment metric; a data check fits his lane.

hits.name: Dennis Porter
hits.text: This is not good for Republicans. Democrats were underestimated in 100% of the close Senate races in 2022. When history repeats, Democrats will take the majority in the Senate by a wide margin. https://t.co/DofUKk3TR1
hits.hook: This is not good for Republicans. Democrats were underestimated in 100% of the close Senate races in 2022. When history repeats, Democrats will take the majority in the Senate by a wide margin. https:
hits.story: Dennis Porter: Democrats were underestimated in 100% of close 2022 Senate races
hits.draft_en:
'X was underestimated in 100% of close races last cycle, so it will happen again.'

That's one cycle.

Polling errors don't keep the same direction every election.
They move. Pollsters adjust after each miss.

One sample is a story, not a base rate.
Same mistake shows up in $BTC charts all the time.

How many cycles would you want before trusting a pattern like this?
Save this for election night.
hits.draft_quote_en:
One cycle isn't a pattern.

What did polling errors look like across several cycles, and did the direction stay the same? If it flips, 'history repeats' doesn't hold.
hits.video_tip: Bar chart placeholder: polling error by cycle, alternating direction, label 'check the data'; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Stay non-partisan: one cycle of polling misses isn't a base rate; ask for the direction of polling error across several cycles (check historical averages) and compare with prediction market odds.
hits.why_chosen: Fresh, testable base-rate claim from an account he already engages; bridges to sample size and markets vs polls.

hits.name: _Checkmate 🟠🔑⚡☢️🛢️
hits.text:
I was just on the @honestmoneyshow with @BitcoinAnja discussing the psychology of Bitcoiners throughout the cycle.

This is one of my favourite topics, as getting a good read on investor behaviour is imho the secret to navigating cycles with confidence.

https://t.co/qGMMKgerls
hits.hook: I was just on the @honestmoneyshow with @BitcoinAnja discussing the psychology of Bitcoiners throughout the cycle.
hits.story: Checkmate on Bitcoiner psychology across the cycle
hits.draft_en:
Investor behaviour through the cycle sounds soft.
It's actually measurable.

Coins held by long-term holders, profit taking, dormant coins waking up.
It's all on-chain.

Feelings are the story. On-chain data is the receipt.

Which signal do you trust most to tell you where we are in the cycle?
Save this / repost it for the next 'is this the top?' debate.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Good topic. How do you separate psychology from plain liquidity?

On-chain shows what holders did. Does it tell us why, or are we fitting a story after the fact?
hits.video_tip: Split screen: emotion faces on one side, matching on-chain charts on the other; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Ask how much of 'cycle psychology' on-chain data really captures vs liquidity (check LTH supply and spent output profit ratio), and whether it works in real time or only in hindsight.
hits.why_chosen: Fresh post from an on-chain analyst; natural spot for a sharp data question.

hits.text: Cut, hold or hike, the Fed's decision doesn't tell you which way Bitcoin goes next. Across 81 meetings, the median return a week later is close to zero in all three cases, and the distributions look almost identical. https://t.co/1pUwYyuPRh
hits.hook: Cut, hold or hike, the Fed's decision doesn't tell you which way Bitcoin goes next. Across 81 meetings, the median return a week later is close to zero in all three cases, and the distributions look a
hits.story: Fed decisions vs. BTC a week later
hits.draft_en:
FOMC today. ecoinometrics checked 81 Fed meetings.

Cut, hold or hike: the median $BTC return a week later is close to zero in all three cases.

If that holds, trading the decision is mostly noise.
For a spot buyer, the plan you already have matters more than today's headline.

What would you change in your plan, if anything?
Save this for the next Fed day.
hits.draft_quote_en:
This is the base rate most Fed-day posts skip.

One follow-up: is the spread of outcomes also similar, or just the median? A similar median can hide very different tails.
hits.video_tip: Three overlapping distribution curves labeled cut, hold, hike, caption 'spot the difference'; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Build on it: ask whether the tails and volatility after decisions also match, not just the median; a check he can run on the same 81 meetings.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + distribution of $BTC 7-day returns after Fed cuts, holds and hikes (81 meetings, source ecoinometrics, to be checked). Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: FOMC day plus a real base rate; perfect fit for a data-minded reply.

For the first time in history, we have money
hits.hook: The greatest trick of the fiat system wasn't convincing people that inflation is good.
hits.story: Fiat's trick: convincing people there is no alternative
hits.draft_en:
'Money must lose value' gets said like a law of nature.

It's a policy choice. Central banks target about 2% a year.
That still cuts purchasing power in half in roughly 35 years.

$BTC is one alternative.
It comes with its own cost: volatility.

Which risk would you rather manage, slow inflation or fast drawdowns?
If it was useful, a repost helps more people see it.
hits.draft_quote_en:
The point about 'no alternative' is fair. But alternatives come with their own risks.

Inflation is slow and predictable-ish. $BTC drawdowns are fast. The honest pitch shows both.
hits.video_tip: A dollar bill shrinking slowly next to a $BTC line swinging hard; 8s.
hits.reply_angle: Add the trade-off: a 2% target halves purchasing power in about 35 years, while $BTC trades that for volatility; ask which risk people are actually equipped to hold.
hits.why_chosen: Strong claim with high like rate; room for an honest trade-off reply instead of an echo.

virals_narrative: Watchlist scan done (342 originals in 18h, 50 accounts). One card per account.
narrative_synthesis: Late evening after the FOMC: the Fed hold and Warsh's 'inflation is too high' still dominate, alongside Google's earnings miss. Tokenization is the other big thread: 33 US companies object to tokenized versions of their stock on OKX/ICE while Ripple Swell speakers claim $400B tokenized. On $BTC: under 900K left to mine, 6x in six years per CoinMarketCap, corporate buying at 19K BTC/month per River, and Hagerty on adding to the US reserve. Best angle for @ForecastQuant: split data from projection, ask for drawdowns and base rates, $BTC spot only.
